title: Miniature Animation Curve Editor with Bezier Handles Diorama
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that renders a miniature diorama of an animation curve editor with interactive bezier handles in 3D space.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 12) looking at origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera rotation (damping enabled).
- Background color: #1a1a2e (dark navy). Add a subtle grid helper (size 20, divisions 20, color #2a2a4a) on the ground plane.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- The diorama sits on a small 3D platform: a rounded box (10 x 0.3 x 6) with a slightly glossy dark material (#222244) centered at origin.

CURVE EDITOR PANEL (3D):
- Floating above the platform at y=1, render a 3D rectangular panel (8 x 0.1 x 4) with a semi-transparent dark material representing the curve editor background.
- On this panel, draw a coordinate grid using thin LineSegments: 8 vertical lines and 4 horizontal lines in dim cyan (#1a3a4a).
- The X-axis represents time (0 to 1), the Z-axis represents value (0 to 1), mapped onto the panel surface.

BEZIER CURVE:
- Define a cubic bezier curve with 4 control points:
  - P0 (start): panel-local coords (-3.5, 0.1, -1.5) — fixed anchor
  - P1 (handle1): panel-local coords (-1.5, 0.1, 1.5) — draggable
  - P2 (handle2): panel-local coords (1.5, 0.1, -1.0) — draggable
  - P3 (end): panel-local coords (3.5, 0.1, 1.5) — fixed anchor
- Render the bezier curve as a TubeGeometry or thick line (use ~64 segments) in bright cyan (#00ffcc), updated whenever handles move.
- Render thin lines from P0->P1 and P2->P3 (handle tangent lines) in orange (#ff8844).
- Render each control point as a small sphere (radius 0.15): anchors in white, draggable handles in orange.

ANIMATED PREVIEW OBJECT:
- Place a small glowing sphere (radius 0.25, emissive green #00ff88) that travels along the bezier curve over time.
- The sphere completes one loop every 3 seconds, continuously. Its parameter t goes from 0 to 1 and loops.
- A vertical thin line (green) drops from the sphere down to the platform to show its position shadow.

INTERACTION - DRAG HANDLES:
- Implement raycaster-based drag on the two handle spheres (P1 and P2). On mousedown, if a handle is hit, enter drag mode. On mousemove, project the mouse onto the panel plane (y=1.1) and update the handle position, clamping X to [-3.5, 3.5] and Z to [-1.8, 1.8]. On mouseup, release.
- When a handle moves, recompute the bezier curve geometry and update tangent lines.

INTERACTION - KEYBOARD:
- Press 'R' to reset both handles to their default positions.
- Press 'Space' to toggle pause/play of the animated preview sphere.
- Press '1' to select handle P1 (highlight it yellow), press '2' to select handle P2 (highlight it yellow). The other handle returns to orange.
- When a handle is selected, arrow keys Left/Right move it along X by 0.3 units, Up/Down move it along Z by 0.3 units (clamped).

HUD / DOM:
- Add a top-left HUD div showing:
  - 'Curve Editor Diorama' title
  - 'Playing: true/false'
  - 'Selected: None / P1 / P2'
  - 'P1: (x, z)' and 'P2: (x, z)' with 2 decimal places
  - 'Preview t: 0.00' showing current animation parameter
- Add a button 'Reset Handles' at bottom-center that resets handles like pressing R.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- initialized: true when scene is ready
- playing: boolean (animation playing or paused)
- selectedHandle: null | 'P1' | 'P2'
- p1: {x: number, z: number} — current handle P1 position (panel-local)
- p2: {x: number, z: number} — current handle P2 position (panel-local)
- p1Default: {x: -1.5, z: 1.5}
- p2Default: {x: 1.5, z: -1.0}
- previewT: number (0 to 1, current animation parameter)
- curveSegments: number (how many segments the curve mesh has, should be ~64)
- handleDragging: false | 'P1' | 'P2'
- previewPosition: {x, y, z} — world position of the preview sphere
- curveLength: number — approximate length of the bezier curve
- resetCount: number — how many times handles have been reset (starts 0)
physics_constraints: Bezier curve must be a valid cubic bezier computed from 4 control points. Handle positions must remain clamped within panel bounds (X: [-3.5, 3.5], Z: [-1.8, 1.8]). Preview sphere must follow the exact bezier path parameterized by t in [0,1]. Curve length must be positive and finite. Animation parameter t must loop in [0,1].
